title: Karush-Kuhn-Tucker Conditions and Convex Duality in Non-Linear Programming
abstract: We analyze necessary and sufficient conditions for constrained convex optimization.

sections.heading: 1. Convex Functions and Sets
sections.text:
Definition 1.5. A function f: R^n -> R is convex if f(tx + (1-t)y) <= t f(x) + (1-t) f(y) for all t in [0,1].
Example 3. The norm function f(x) = ||x|| is convex.

sections.heading: 2. Optimality Conditions
sections.text:
Lemma 2.5. For convex differentiable f, local minima are global minima.
Theorem 7.1. Theorem 7.1 follows from Lemma 2.5. Under Slater's condition, x* is optimal if and only if there exist KKT multipliers satisfying primal and dual feasibility.
Proof of Theorem 7.1. Apply Definition 1.5 and Lemma 2.5 via hyper-plane separation.
Corollary 7.2. By Theorem 7.1, strong duality holds for strictly feasible convex problems.
